newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan closes up at a five-week high vs US dollar.
newsitem.headline: Yuan closes up at a five-week high vs US dollar.

text.p: The Chinese yuan rose for the fourth day in a row to close at a five-week high of 8.2967 against the U.S. dollar on Thurday from Wednesday's 8.2977 with intervention by the central bank decreasing, traders said.

The local unit opened lower at 8.2978 and hit an intra-day low of 8.2980 early in the session. It then rose to move around 8.2975 for most of the session before rising further to end at an intra-day high.
Trading was dull, with most done at 8.2975, traders said.
Dealers said reduced intervention by the People's Bank of China promoted active buying for the yuan.

"Although the yuan has risen a lot in the past four days, there was little sign that the central bank would force it back to the 8.3000 level," said one dealer. "The current rises were still in a range which the central bank could control."
He said he expected the central bank not to intervene actively in the market until the yuan rises further towards the next high of 8.2960 which was set on November 12.
Dealers expect the yuan to move around 8.2970 on Friday.
The yuan closed slightly up at 7.2900 from 7.3000 against 100 Japanese yen and up at an intra-day high of 1.0710 from 1.0727 against the Hong Kong dollar.
